summary: Restoration is framed at EU level: restoration measures should cover at least 20% of EU land areas and 20% of sea areas by 2030, with measures in place by 2050 for all ecosystems that need restoration. Separately, peatland and wetland rewetting has a stated mitigation potential of 51–54 Mt CO2-eq per year, and ecologically appropriate reforestation with sustainable forest management 8–235 Mt CO2-eq per year. Conservation and cross-sector LULUCF pledges set Union net removals at 310 Mt CO2 by 2030 (also expressed as a −310 Mt CO2-eq carbon-sink target); Hungary’s listed national LULUCF target is −934 Kt CO2eq for 2030. Agriculture addresses fertiliser-use efficiency, with 19 Mt CO2-eq per year of mitigation potential. These are EU-wide or emissions-based figures, not Hungarian area commitments; Hungary’s land-cover shares are 68.2% agriculture, 19.1% forest, 6.9% grassland and 0.5% wetland. The source’s peer-country figures are not attributed to Hungary.
